src.explanation: Beta-2 receptors mediate bronchodilation, so blocking them raises airway resistance. Betaxolol is the beta-1 selective option on this list; carteolol, timolol and levobunolol are non-selective.

items.html: Prazosin reflex tachycardia. The reflex tachycardia with prazosin is mild, possibly because of some central sympatholytic activity and because prazosin dilates both arteries and veins.

src.question: How is the reflex tachycardia seen with prazosin described?
src.explanation: Prazosin causes only mild reflex tachycardia, possibly because of some central sympatholytic activity and because it dilates both arteries and veins.

items.html: Alpha-1 blocker names. The -zosin suffix marks the alpha-1 selective antagonists prazosin, terazosin and doxazosin; tamsulosin is the alpha-1A selective agent.

src.question: Which of these drugs is an alpha-1 blocker?
src.explanation: The -zosin suffix marks the alpha-1 selective antagonists: prazosin, terazosin and doxazosin, with tamsulosin as the alpha-1A selective agent.

items.section_title: 3.9 · Objectives 9–10 — The treatment algorithm, monitoring and patient education
items.html: Hypertension after a myocardial infarction. A history of myocardial infarction is a reason to start a beta blocker early, because beta blockade protects ischemic myocardium and protects against recurrent infarction.

src.question: A 61-year-old with hypertension had a myocardial infarction last year. Which class should generally be used initially?
src.explanation: A history of myocardial infarction is a reason to start a beta blocker early; beta blockade protects ischemic myocardium and protects against recurrent infarction.

items.html: Nimodipine. Nimodipine is the dihydropyridine approved for subarachnoid hemorrhage; the other dihydropyridines are approved for hypertension with or without angina.

src.question: Which dihydropyridine is approved for subarachnoid hemorrhage?
src.explanation: Nimodipine's approved indication is subarachnoid hemorrhage, unlike the other dihydropyridines, which are approved for hypertension with or without angina.

items.html: Calcium channel blocker gynecomastia. Gynecomastia is more likely with nifedipine than with diltiazem, whereas gingival hyperplasia is shared across the class.

src.question: Which calcium channel blocker is more likely than diltiazem to cause gynecomastia?
src.explanation: Gynecomastia is listed with the comparison that nifedipine exceeds diltiazem; gingival hyperplasia is shared across the class.

items.html: Diltiazem and tacrolimus. The tacrolimus level rises when diltiazem is started: non-dihydropyridines inhibit CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein, and tacrolimus and cyclosporine are on both lists, so their levels rise.

src.question: A transplant recipient taking tacrolimus is started on diltiazem. What is expected to happen to the tacrolimus level?
src.explanation: Non-dihydropyridines inhibit CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein, and tacrolimus and cyclosporine are on both lists, so their levels rise.

items.html: Calcium channel blockers in heart failure. Heart failure is a relative contraindication to the non-dihydropyridines because they suppress contractility; amlodipine, a dihydropyridine approved for hypertension, has little effect on contractility and avoids this.

src.question: A patient with hypertension also has heart failure. Which calcium channel blocker avoids the relative contraindication in heart failure?
src.explanation: Heart failure is a relative contraindication to the non-dihydropyridines because they suppress contractility; amlodipine, a dihydropyridine approved for hypertension, has little effect on contractility.

items.html: Losartan and hyperkalemia. Hyperkalemia with angiotensin receptor blockers is linked to renal disease and potassium-sparing diuretics, both of which keep potassium in, so adding a potassium-sparing diuretic to losartan most increases the risk.

src.question: Which drug added to losartan most increases the risk of hyperkalemia?
src.explanation: Hyperkalemia with angiotensin receptor blockers is linked to renal disease and potassium-sparing diuretics, both of which keep potassium in.

items.html: Ramipril class. Ramipril is an ACE (angiotensin-converting enzyme) inhibitor; the -pril suffix marks the class, which also includes lisinopril, enalapril, benazepril and quinapril.

src.question: A patient's medication list includes ramipril. To which drug class does it belong?
src.explanation: The -pril suffix marks an ACE (angiotensin-converting enzyme) inhibitor; ramipril sits alongside lisinopril, enalapril, benazepril and quinapril.

items.html: Renin release and renal perfusion. Renin release increases when renal perfusion falls: the renal baroreceptor responds to stretch of the afferent arteriole, so less perfusion means more renin. Sympathetic activity at beta-1 receptors raises it too.

src.question: What happens to renin release when renal perfusion falls?
src.explanation: The renal baroreceptor responds to stretch of the afferent arteriole: less perfusion, more renin. Sympathetic activity at beta-1 receptors raises it too.

items.section_title: 4.8 · Objective 3 — Which class for which lipid
items.html: Largest HDL rise. Nicotinic acid (niacin) raises HDL (high-density lipoprotein) cholesterol by 15 to 35%, the largest rise of any class; fibrates follow at 10 to 35%.

src.question: Which class produces the largest rise in HDL (high-density lipoprotein) cholesterol?
src.explanation: Niacin raises HDL by 15 to 35%, the largest rise of any class; fibrates follow at 10 to 35%.

items.section_title: 4.8 · Objective 3 — Which class for which lipid
items.html: Largest LDL lowering. Statins lower LDL (low-density lipoprotein) cholesterol by 18 to 55%, the most of any class; they are the most efficacious and first line.

src.question: Which class lowers LDL (low-density lipoprotein) cholesterol the most?
src.explanation: Statins lower LDL by 18 to 55%, the most of any class; they are the most efficacious and first line.

items.html: Niacin and hepatic VLDL production. Niacin decreases mobilization of free fatty acids from fat (adipose tissue), so less fatty acid is mobilized and the liver makes less triglyceride, VLDL (very low-density lipoprotein) and apo B; LDL falls and HDL rises.

src.question: How does niacin reduce hepatic VLDL (very low-density lipoprotein) production?
src.key: Less fatty acid mobilized from fat
src.explanation: Niacin decreases mobilization of free fatty acids from adipose tissue, so the liver makes less triglyceride, VLDL and apo B; LDL falls and HDL rises.

items.html: Ezetimibe systemic exposure. Enterohepatic recirculation limits systemic exposure: ezetimibe and its active glucuronide metabolite circulate enterohepatically, returning the drug to its site of action.

src.question: What limits ezetimibe's systemic exposure?
src.explanation: Ezetimibe and its active glucuronide metabolite circulate enterohepatically, returning the drug to its site of action and limiting systemic exposure.

items.html: Shared end result of LDL-lowering drugs. Statins, ezetimibe, bile acid sequestrants and PCSK9 inhibitors lower LDL (low-density lipoprotein) through more active hepatic LDL receptors: statins and resins upregulate them, ezetimibe raises their expression by cutting cholesterol supply, and PCSK9 inhibitors keep them active longer.

src.question: Statins, ezetimibe, bile acid sequestrants and PCSK9 inhibitors lower LDL (low-density lipoprotein) through which shared end result?
src.explanation: Statins and resins upregulate them, ezetimibe raises their expression by cutting cholesterol supply, and PCSK9 inhibitors keep them active longer.

items.html: Statin muscle toxicity. Rhabdomyolysis is the most severe muscle toxicity of statins; it is rare, whereas myalgia and myopathy (0.2 to 0.4%) are more common. Muscle toxicity requires stopping the statin.

src.question: What is the most severe muscle toxicity of statins?
src.explanation: Myalgia and myopathy (0.2 to 0.4%) are more common; rhabdomyolysis is rare but the most severe, and muscle toxicity requires stopping the statin.

items.section_title: 1.4 · Objectives 1–3 — Allergy and the red eye
items.html: Topical ocular vasoconstrictors. Locally in the eye they act on alpha 1 receptors, which constrict the conjunctival vessels; systemically these imidazolines target alpha 2 instead, which is what makes an accidental ingestion dangerous.

src.question: Topical vasoconstrictors act on which receptor LOCALLY in the eye?
src.explanation: Locally alpha 1, which constricts the conjunctival vessels. Systemically these imidazolines target alpha 2 instead, which is what makes an accidental ingestion dangerous.

items.html: Ophthalmic non-steroidal anti-inflammatories. Ketorolac blocks cyclooxygenase, stopping conversion of arachidonic acid to prostaglandins and thromboxanes; the mechanism is the same whether the drug is taken for a headache or put in the eye.

src.question: Which ophthalmic class blocks cyclooxygenase, stopping conversion of arachidonic acid to prostaglandins and thromboxanes?
src.explanation: The ophthalmic non-steroidals. The mechanism is the same whether the drug is taken for a headache or put in the eye.

items.html: Ophthalmia neonatorum prophylaxis. Erythromycin, as the 0.5% ointment, is the ophthalmic antibiotic used for newborn prophylaxis and for superficial conjunctival or corneal infection.

src.question: Which ophthalmic antibiotic is used for prophylaxis of ophthalmia neonatorum?
src.explanation: The 0.5% ointment, for superficial conjunctival or corneal infection and for newborn prophylaxis.

items.html: Azithromycin ophthalmic use. Azithromycin is considerably more expensive and given less frequently (twice a day against four or more times for erythromycin), but the cost keeps it from being used as often clinically.

src.question: Which ophthalmic antibiotic is considerably more expensive and given less frequently, so it is not used as often clinically?
src.explanation: Twice a day against four or more for erythromycin, but the cost keeps it off the shelf.

items.section_title: 1.1 · Objective 4 — Getting a drug into the eye, and out again
items.html: Intravitreal delivery. Intravitreal injection or device circumvents absorption entirely for an immediate local effect; it is used for endophthalmitis, retinitis and age-related macular degeneration, and its limitation is retinal toxicity.

src.question: Which route of ocular drug delivery circumvents absorption entirely for an immediate local effect?
src.explanation: Used for endophthalmitis, retinitis and age-related macular degeneration. Its limitation is retinal toxicity.

items.html: Diltiazem and simvastatin. Diltiazem raises simvastatin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4; non-dihydropyridines inhibit CYP3A4, raising atorvastatin, lovastatin and simvastatin.

src.question: Which calcium channel blocker RAISES SIMVASTATIN levels by inhibiting CYP3A4?
src.explanation: Non-dihydropyridines inhibit CYP3A4, raising atorvastatin, lovastatin and simvastatin.

items.html: Beta blocker for migraine prophylaxis. Propranolol (with timolol) is used for migraine prophylaxis at low dose; the mechanism is uncertain.

src.question: Which beta blocker is used for MIGRAINE PROPHYLAXIS?
src.explanation: Propranolol (with timolol) is used for migraine prophylaxis at low dose; the mechanism is uncertain.

items.html: Cholinergic agonist in the surgical setting. Acetylcholine is the surgical agent among the three cholinergic agonists.

src.question: Which cholinergic agonist is used in the SURGICAL setting?
src.explanation: The surgical agent among the three cholinergic agonists.

items.html: Rosuvastatin metabolism. Rosuvastatin's major metabolic route is minimal CYP, so CYP3A4 inhibitors affect it least, unlike the CYP3A4 statins.

src.question: Which statin has MINIMAL CYP metabolism, so CYP3A4 inhibitors affect it least?
src.explanation: Rosuvastatin's major metabolic route is listed as minimal CYP, unlike the CYP3A4 statins.

items.section_title: 1.1 · Objective 4 — Getting a drug into the eye, and out again
items.html: Intravitreal treatment of endophthalmitis. Intravitreal injection or device circumvents absorption entirely for an immediate local effect, with a potential sustained effect too; its limitation is retinal toxicity.

src.question: A 57-year-old needs treatment for endophthalmitis with an immediate local effect. Which route achieves this by circumventing absorption entirely?
src.explanation: with a potential sustained effect too. Its limitation is retinal toxicity.

items.html: Pilocarpine in younger patients. Pilocarpine is particularly poorly tolerated in younger patients because miosis blurs vision: fixed small pupils, myopia and visual disturbance, and compliance suffers for it.

src.question: A 26-year-old finds his vision blurs badly on pilocarpine. Why is this class particularly poorly tolerated in younger patients?
src.explanation: Correct — fixed small pupils, myopia and visual disturbance, and compliance suffers for it.

items.html: Newborn ophthalmia neonatorum prophylaxis. Erythromycin ointment is the named agent for prophylaxis against ophthalmia neonatorum, and it is inexpensive.

src.question: A newborn needs prophylaxis against ophthalmia neonatorum. Which agent?
src.explanation: It is the named agent for newborn prophylaxis, and it is inexpensive.

items.section_title: 5.7 · Objectives 1–7 — Acute coronary syndrome: aspirin, nitrates, beta blockers, morphine
items.html: Beta blockers in acute coronary syndrome: intravenously first, then orally. The traditional sequence is an intravenous beta blocker followed by an oral one. Current guidelines favor oral therapy within the first day and avoid the intravenous route when there is heart failure, low output or a risk of shock.

src.question: In the traditional approach to acute coronary syndrome, how is a beta blocker given?
src.explanation: Correct. The traditional sequence is an intravenous beta blocker followed by an oral one. Current guidelines favor oral therapy within the first day and avoid the intravenous route when there is heart failure, low output or a risk of shock.

items.html: Warn patients starting a nitrate about dizziness when standing up. Nitrates cause orthostatic hypotension, so patients are warned about light-headedness on standing.

src.question: What should patients starting a nitrate be warned about?
src.explanation: Correct. Nitrates cause orthostatic hypotension, so patients are warned about light-headedness on standing.

items.html: Replace opened nitroglycerin tablets. The traditional counseling is to replace opened tablets about every 3 to 6 months so that a potent tablet is ready in an emergency. Current labeling ties expiry to the printed date when the tablets stay in the tightly closed original glass bottle.

src.question: A 70-year-old man with stable angina opened his bottle of sublingual nitroglycerin tablets eight months ago. He keeps it in the original container in a bedroom drawer and has used it twice. In the traditional counseling, what should he be told about the tablets?
src.key: Replace them with a fresh supply
src.explanation: Correct. The traditional counseling is to replace opened tablets about every 3 to 6 months so that a potent tablet is ready in an emergency. Current labeling ties expiry to the printed date when the tablets stay in the tightly closed original glass bottle.

items.section_title: 5.5 · Objectives 1–3 and 7 — Add-on therapy, comorbid conditions and variant angina
items.html: After a myocardial infarction, calcium channel blockers are the class to avoid. The traditional comorbidity table says to avoid calcium channel blockers after an infarction and to prefer a beta blocker. Current practice is less absolute and allows a non-dihydropyridine when a beta blocker cannot be used.

src.question: A 63-year-old man with stable exertional angina had a myocardial infarction three years ago. Heart rate is 70 beats per minute and blood pressure is 128/78 mmHg. He has no asthma and no conduction disease. In the traditional comorbidity-based approach, which class is best avoided?
src.explanation: Correct. The traditional comorbidity table says to avoid calcium channel blockers after an infarction and to prefer a beta blocker. Current practice is less absolute and allows a non-dihydropyridine when a beta blocker cannot be used.

items.html: Propranolol is a non-cardioselective beta blocker. Non-cardioselective beta blockers such as propranolol are to be avoided in asthma.

src.question: Which drug is non-cardioselective, so it is avoided in patients with asthma?
src.explanation: Correct. Non-cardioselective beta blockers such as propranolol are to be avoided in asthma.

items.html: Opened nitroglycerin tablets are replaced on a schedule because the drug degrades. Nitroglycerin is unstable, and exposure to light or moisture breaks it down so it may not work when needed; that is the reason for the traditional 3 to 6 month replacement and for keeping the tablets in the original container.

src.question: Why are opened nitroglycerin tablets replaced on a schedule?
src.key: Light and moisture degrade the drug
src.explanation: Correct. Nitroglycerin is unstable, and exposure to light or moisture breaks it down so it may not work when needed; that is the reason for the traditional 3 to 6 month replacement and for keeping the tablets in the original container.
